articleTitle: Blockchain Sharding Model for Increasing The Efficiency of The Global Car Rental Industry Based on Blockchain Technology
abstract: The global car rental industry is an economic sector that involves providing car rental services for a certain period to consumers spread across several countries. This industry includes the provision of various types of vehicles, from economy cars to luxury cars, and this industry is experiencing significant growth and has bright potential, especially with the trend of increasing demand for luxury cars in several markets. Previous research shows that blockchain technology can increase the transparency and security of transactions at car rental companies. However, the large number of parties involved and the spread of car rental locations in several different countries contribute to the high costs of implementing blockchain technology. So, the problem statement of this research is how the blockchain sharding concept can increase the efficiency of the process of implementing blockchain technology in the global car rental industry. The research uses qualitative methods to identify problems in implementing blockchain technology in the global car rental industry. A qualitative approach through literature reviews is also used to find more effective blockchain methods. The result of this research is an adopted blockchain sharding model in the global car rental industry. At the end of the article, a simulation using the Ganache is explained.

articleTitle: Improving Search Efficiency for Myanmar-Korean ICT Standard Terms Dictionary Using Information Retrieval Methods
abstract: The Myanmar-Korean ICT Standard Online Dictionary, which incorporates advanced artificial intelligence, bridges the linguistic and technical divide in the realm of Information and Communication Technology (ICT). This study focuses on enhancing the search efficiency for Myanmar-Korean ICT Standard Terms by leveraging information retrieval methods: TF-IDF, BM25, and Latent Semantic Analysis (LSA). A dataset of 26,335 Korean Standard ICT Terms, sourced from the Korean Authority of ICT Standardization, was migrated and adapted to the Myanmar context. The system supports multilingual searches and indexing in Myanmar, English, and Korean, enabling more effective term retrieval. Key features include a user-driven customization mechanism for suggesting, editing, and approving new terms, as well as periodic updates facilitated by a Django Rest Framework-based backend. Statistical analysis tools monitor user contributions to enhance collaboration and continuous improvement. This research aims to improve accessibility to ICT terminology for professionals, educators, and students, fostering greater cross-linguistic understanding and promoting knowledge exchange between Myanmar and Korean-speaking communities.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison on Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) in Fog-Cloud Workflow Task Scheduling
abstract: In future, most of the electronic devices will be smart or Internet-of-Things (IoT) devices. These devices will be applicable and occupied in organizations, offices and homes, etc. A huge amount of data (big data) from their sensors needs to process real-time data or in a specified time with low latency. Fog computing was a solution to process these data faster because it is processed at fog nodes which are nearer the users rather than cloud nodes in spite of limited computing resources. To complete the tasks in few times and reduce the delay time, effective task scheduling is also required in Fog-Cloud environment. This paper presents and analyzes the performance of workflow task scheduling algorithms: Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Genetic Algorithm (GA) with different workflow settings (Montage, Cybershake, Epigenomics, Inspiral, and Sipht). As the Quality of Service (QoS) parameters in terms of makespan, cost, execution time, energy consumption and so on will be shown in terms of experimental results.

articleTitle: Online Learning Certification System using Blockchain Technology
abstract: In the educational 4.0 era, the online education system has been developed in modern society changing. Online learning will be as valuable as formal learning. Online education has allowed people to learn a new skill from their homes comfortably to overcome issues such as geographic limitations, and time and cost constraints in traditional learning. Although online education is a social benefit, there are some problems due to the lack of trust and fake certificates. To overcome these critical problems, blockchain technology is introduced. Blockchain technology can offer significant advantages to the effectiveness of online education. Blockchain technology is applied in many areas such as the supply chain management, voting system, finance and banking, IoT, medical treatment, and education. The paper presents the blockchain-based smart contracts is used in an online learning platform. Blockchain records the learning histories in a distributed blockchain ledger. It is expected that blockchain-based online learning would be not only the improvement of the quality of the education system but also prevent fraudulent activities to produce fake certificates.

articleTitle: A Review on Reinforcement Learning Based Task Scheduling in Edge Computing
abstract: By bringing computational operations closer to data sources, edge computing lowers latency and boosts productivity. Task scheduling is made more difficult by issues including resource heterogeneity, fluctuating workloads, and strict latency requirements. With its adaptive, real-time optimization capabilities, reinforcement learning (RL) has become a viable option. With an emphasis on RL techniques like Q-learning, Deep Q-Learning, and Actor-Critic models, this study examines important job scheduling approaches in edge computing, including heuristic, optimization-based, and RL-driven methods. These techniques are excellent at reducing latency, increasing energy efficiency, and allocating resources as efficiently as possible. The paper emphasizes the revolutionary potential of RL for task scheduling in edge contexts by looking at advancements, techniques, and future prospects. It also emphasizes the significance of hybrid approaches that integrate RL with other methodologies to solve scalability, heterogeneity, and computing complexity, paving the path for novel, efficient solutions in distributed systems.

articleTitle: Concurrency Control with Timestamp and Recovery Using Passive Replication
abstract: Efficient concurrency control and robust recovery mechanisms are essential for ensuring consistency and availability in group work data-sharing systems. This paper introduces a novel approach combining timestamp-based concurrency control and passive replication to address the challenges of concurrent transaction management and system failure recovery. The timestamp-based method enforces a strict ordering of transactions, preventing conflicts and ensuring consistency across shared data. Passive replication enhances fault tolerance by maintaining synchronized backup copies, enabling efficient recovery with minimal system overhead. Unlike active replication, the proposed method reduces network and processing costs while maintaining high availability and reliability. Experimental results demonstrate that the approach significantly improves system performance by minimizing transaction conflicts, ensuring data integrity, and providing fast recovery during failures. This solution is particularly effective in distributed environments, supporting scalable and reliable collaboration in group work scenarios. This paper presents the implementation and evaluation of a concurrency control mechanism using timestamps combined with a recovery strategy based on passive replication in distributed databases. The proposed method ensures serializability by ordering transactions according to their timestamp, thereby minimizing conflicts and avoiding deadlocks. Recovery is achieved through passive replication, where secondary replicas maintain the latest committed state, enabling seamless failover during failures. Experimental results demonstrate an average transaction time of 150 ms, a 95% conflict resolution success rate, and a failover time of 50 ms. The approach exhibits improved throughput and fault tolerance, making it a viable solution for distributed systems requiring high consistency and availability.

articleTitle: Inflow Prediction of Lower Paunglaung Dam for Water Resource Management
abstract: Reservoir dams play a vital role in the national economy and social development of any country, such as flood control, power generation, irrigation and water supply. The Lower Paunglaung Dam, the largest multipurpose dam in Myanmar, is facing difficulties in managing its water resources. Lower Paunglaung Dam and its weir were mainly constructed to irrigate agricultural land as well as to generate hydropower. Predicting the inflow rate precisely is therefore essential for managing water resources since it aids in planning for floods, droughts, and the production of electricity in the Nay Pyi Taw region. Moreover, climate change impacts are more significantly affecting the safety of dams. In order to prevent flood damage and maintain a steady supply of water from water resources, accurate dam inflow estimates are becoming more and more important in the face of climate change. In order to estimate dam inflow, this study used historical data from the previous 20 years. A deep learning model, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) is used in this system to predict the inflow of Lower Paunglaung Dam in the Paunglaung River watershed in Myanmar. Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), accuracy, number of epochs are taken into account for assessing the effectiveness and performance of the suggested inflow prediction model.

articleTitle: IoT-Enabled Wireless Sensor Network for Dam Safety Management
abstract: Dams play a vital role in water management, energy production, and flood control. However, their structural integrity and operational safety require continuous monitoring and management. Traditional dam safety systems often involve manual inspections, which can be time-consuming and inefficient. The advent of the Internet of Things (IoT) has revolutionized monitoring and management practices across various industries. This paper explores the development and implementation of a Dam Safety Management System (DSMS) using IoT. The system leverages sensors, cloud computing, and real-time data analytics to enhance dam safety, streamline operations, and mitigate risks. The proposed system aims to provide accurate, timely insights into dam performance, enabling proactive interventions to prevent disasters.

articleTitle: Real-time Flood Monitoring System using Internet of Things in Urban
abstract: Flooding is one of the most common natural disasters in the world. While prevention is impossible, damage can be minimized with early detection. So, a reliable, real-time flood monitoring system is more urgent than ever. This paper presents the design and implementation of a real-time flood monitoring system using the Internet of Things (IoT) combined with the ThingSpeak Cloud Platform. The proposed system collects data from a water level sensor, a temperature sensor, and a humidity sensor and transmits the information to a cloud-based platform for analysis and visualization. The system provides early warnings and real-time updates to authorities and residents, enabling timely action to mitigate the impact of flooding. This paper combines hardware and software components to notify the appropriate authorities via email in addition to displaying brief alerts on ThingSpeak. Then, it notifies decision-makers via email alert for flood mitigation infrastructure, aiming to take appropriate action to lessen the impact of flooding.

Author Keywords: early warning system and Flood monitoring

articleTitle: Developing Phrase-Based SMT for low-Resource Language Translation: Myanmar and Tedim Chin Language
abstract: This paper presents an initial evaluation of a translation system developed to address the linguistic gap between the Myanmar and Tedim Chin languages. As part of this project, we have also compiled a parallel corpus for Myanmar-Tedim Chin, containing around 50,000 sentences sourced from the UCSY corpus. Translation involves converting the symbols or characters of one writing system into those of another, with the aim of preserving the original pronunciation as closely as possible. For the Myanmar and Tedim Chin languages, accurate translation is particularly challenging due to the complexity of their writing systems and the limited availability of relevant data. In this study, we perform statistical experiments using the Phrase-Based Statistical Machine Translation (PBSMT) model, employing 5-gram language models during the decoding phase. We conduct experiments with a test set of 1,000 sentences and a development set of 7,000 sentences from the newly created dataset. To assess the performance of the translation system, we use the Bilingual Evaluation Understudy (BLEU) score, evaluating both Myanmar-to-Tedim Chin and Tedim Chin-to-Myanmar translation directions.

articleTitle: ChildASR: Child Automatic Speech Recognition for Myanmar Language
abstract: This paper presents the child automatic speech recognition (ChildASR) for Myanmar language. Many researchers have completed the recognition system for adult speakers and made significant progress in every language. However, child speech recognition is rare to develop and a challenge in a variety of application scenarios especially in Myanmar Language. This work is the first attempt for Primary level students and benefits for the children with dyslexia and other learning impairments. In this study, a recognizer is built for Myanmar child speech by using the Gaussian Mixture Model based Hidden Markov Model (GMM-HMM). This work investigates the effectiveness of variation on language model and the variation of number of senones and Gaussian densities on Myanmar child speech. To implement this work, text data totaling 2,682 sentences is obtained from Primary Myanmar Textbook. By using this text, speech data is recorded with children. The speech dataset contains ~5 hours that are recorded with 3 male speakers and 7 female speakers. Word Error Rate (WER) is used to assess the performance of GMM-HMM recognizer. According to these experiments, the lowest error rate reaches to 14.45% using a speaker adaptive HMM-GMM model.

articleTitle: The Implementation of Enterprise Resource Planning in Small Medium Enterprise: A Systematic Literature Review
abstract: Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) is essential in a large company today, this is because of its benefits which make it easier for top management or decision makers to make company business decisions, operational efficiency, and development of the company's business itself. Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) is synonymous with large-scale companies because the costs of implementing and designing Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) are generally large-scale. However, many Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) use or implement Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) in their business. This research investigates the impact of success and what factors make Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) successfully implemented in Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs). This study uses a systematic literature review method using the PRISMA method and Google Scholar as data sources or previous articles. The research collected 30 articles which were analyzed, the results of data analysis or previous articles found that ERP has been widely used in many Small and Medium Enterprises with varying success impacts and various implementation success factors such as Top Management Support, ERP utilization strategy, Company Culture, and many Others come from various Small Medium Enterprise (SMES) industries. This study is intended to provide information or insight into the evaluation or development of the implementation of Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) in Small and Medium Enterprise (SMEs) so that it can reconcile the goals and ways for SMEs to successfully gain benefits from Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) in the future.

articleTitle: Effect of Process Design Corner Variations on Threshold Voltage of MOSFET I-V Characteristic Curves
abstract: Threshold voltage variation affects circuit reliability, power efficiency, switching speed, and device performance. The process design corner, the concentration of doping, the potential of the surface, the length of the channel, the thickness of the oxide, the fluctuation of random dopants, the temperature, and other characteristics all have an impact on threshold voltage. Although a wide range of factors is employed, process design corner analysis is most effective in digital electronics because it demonstrates how modifications to the process have a direct impact on the rate at which transistors transition between logic states. The behaviors and threshold voltages of p-channel metal oxide semiconductor field-effect transistors (PMOS) and n-channel metal oxide semiconductor field effect transistors (NMOS) are examined based on the transfer (input) and drain (output) characteristic curves with different drain-to-source and gate-to-source voltages. Understanding the behavior of PMOS and NMOS transistors in the cutoff, linear, and saturation regions is crucial for the design and analysis of analog and digital circuits. The transfer and drain characteristic curves are utilized to analyze the threshold voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</inf>) using several process design corners, including monte carlo (mc), typical test (tt), fast-fast (ff), slow-slow (ss), fast-slow (fs), and slow-fast (sf). Cadence Virtuoso software has been used to numerically investigate the electrical properties of the p-channel and n-channel MOSFETs. With the lowest threshold voltage value among several process design corners, the fast-fast (ff) process design corner enables metal oxide semiconductor field-effect transistors (MOSFETs) to switch on and off more quickly.

articleTitle: Enhance the Digital Transformation in Hotel Groups Through Digital Marketing, Online Reviews, and Service Excellent
abstract: This study aims to investigate the influence of Digital Marketing, Online Reviews, and Service Excellent on Digital Transformation in the hotel group in Central Java. This research uses a survey method with primary data collection from hotel workers. The independent variables in this research are Digital Marketing, Online Reviews, and Service Excellent, while the dependent variable is Digital Transformation. The sample of this study consists of hotel workers who work in various hotels in Central Java by sampling eleven Azana management hotels in Central Java. To determine how the independent variables affect the dependent variable, quantitative research will be used to analyses the collected data. It is anticipated that the study’s findings will enhance comprehension of the significance of the digital marketing, online reviews, and service excellent in improving Digital Transformation in the hotel group in Central Java.

articleTitle: Sentiment Classification of Fine-Tuned mBERT for Myanmar Cosmetic Domain
abstract: Nowadays, sentiment analysis is the crucial task for the feedback of customer review on social media, business organization, and very popular between the market researcher. It becomes an important in making decision for business owners because they want to know the feedback of their products. Sentiment analysis classifies the polarities into positive, negative, or neutral classes. Recent advances in deep learning, particularly transformer-based models, have significantly enhanced the performance of sentiment analysis across various languages. This paper explores sentiment classification using the Multilingual Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (mBERT) on the user review comment that are collected from YouTube channels, Facebook and Tiktok applications written in Myanmar language. Different from BERT transformer, mBERT support 104 languages including Myanmar language. By leveraging the pre-trained mBERT architecture, the study demonstrates significant improvements in classifying Myanmar text into sentiment classification task. Experimental results show the effectiveness of fine-tuning for low-resource languages like Myanmar. The model achieves state-of-the-art performance on a manually annotated dataset by comparing the accuracy on both BERT and mBERT on customized cosmetic dataset.

articleTitle: Utilization of Artificial Intelligence Technology to Improve Programming Skills of Students of Computer Science and Information Systems Department
abstract: In the contemporary digital age, the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into educational practices has garnered significant attention, particularly within the domain of programming education. AI-powered tools offer the potential to streamline the learning process, enabling students to acquire knowledge and skills more efficiently. By automating tasks such as code generation, debugging, and plagiarism detection, AI can alleviate the cognitive load associated with programming, thereby fostering a more engaging and productive learning experience. This study aims to investigate the specific impact of AI on students' programming knowledge and academic performance. Through an online survey administered to a diverse sample of Indonesian university students, this research explores the extent to which AI adoption influences factors such as motivation, self-efficacy, and perceived usefulness. The Information Adoption Model (IAM) serves as the theoretical framework for analysing the collected data. Structural Equation Modelling (SEM) is employed to assess the hypothesized relationships between AI usage and various academic outcomes. The findings of this study are expected to provide valuable insights into the efficacy of AI in enhancing programming education and inform the development of effective AI-integrated learning strategies.

articleTitle: Multi-Object Tracking framework with YOLOv9 Detector and DeepSORT Algorithm based on Generalized Intersection over Union (GIOU)
abstract: Multi-object tracking (MOT) systems are crucial in various real-life applications, including smart video surveillance, traffic monitoring, robotics, sports analytics, customer behavior analysis, and drone control. Despite their widespread use, MOT faces persistent challenges, such as occlusion, ID switching, variations in lighting, background interference, and high object similarity. Deep learning methods like Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN), Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and DeepSORT are commonly employed to address these issues. This research proposes a Multi-Object Tracking framework by combination of the multi-object detector, YOLOv9 and a DeepSORT algorithm based on Generalized Intersection over Union (GIoU) metric to tackle ID switching and occlusion challenges, ultimately improving multi-object tracking accuracy on MOT 16 datasets. Results of the proposed system are compared with the results of the DeepSORT algorithm based on Intersection over Union (IoU) metric. According to the experiment result, the proposed system can track multi-objects more accurately than the DeepSORT based on IoU metric.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Impact of Applied Sampling Algorithm on CNN and LSTM Models for Credit Card Fraud Analysis
abstract: This study performs a comparative analysis of credit card fraud detection using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks on highly imbalanced datasets, with a focus on the impact of a applied sampling algorithm to address class imbalance. Detecting fraudulent transactions is particularly challenging due to the rare occurrence of fraud, leading to poor performance in traditional models. The research evaluates both CNN and LSTM models with and without the sampling algorithm, where the algorithm aims to balance the dataset by enhancing the representation of the minority fraudulent class. CNN is used for automatic feature extraction, while LSTM captures sequential dependencies within transaction data. Experimental results reveal the performance improvements brought by the sampling algorithm, showing increased precision, recall, and F1-score in detecting fraud. The comparison also highlights the differences in how CNN and LSTM perform under imbalanced conditions, as well as the specific advantages of using the applied sampling algorithm, ultimately offering insights into optimizing fraud detection models in the presence of class imbalance.

articleTitle: Fault-Tolerance Model using Stochastic in Blockchain Technique
abstract: Information Technology plays a crucial role in all business scenarios, where ensuring business continuity is vital for every customer who relies on consistent service patterns. This paper is divided into two main sections. The first section addresses the importance of implementing a fault-tolerance model tailored to customer needs. The second section discusses the utilization of tools such as PIPE. The system's behavior is measured using a Markov Stochastic Petri Net (MSPN) model. To measure the structure’s availability, we conducted both numerical derivation and simulations using the PIPE tool. The findings demonstrate that the results obtained from both numerical derivations and simulations are consistent, affirming the reliability of the new model in assessing system availability.

articleTitle: Innovative Validation of Spectrum Analysis and Accurate Dose Measurement for Some Standard Gamma Sources Using RADEAGLE Device and PHITS Simulation
abstract: The spectrum analysis and radiation dose rate determination were carried out by PHITS (Particle of Heavy Iron Transport Code System) simulation calculation and measurement by RADEAGLE (Radiation Equipment for Advanced Gamma-ray Laboratory Evaluation) for precise spectra data and radiation dose calculations. Spectrum analysis and radiation dose estimation have been calculated for some standard gamma radiation sources, <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">241</sup>Am (~368.23 kBq), <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">226</sup>Ra (~27.46 kBq), <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">22</sup>Na (~3.98 kBq), <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">137</sup>Cs (~27.46 kBq) and <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60</sup>Co (~13.39 kBq), which were used for application in academic research work at the Nuclear Physics Laboratory. RADEAGLE device, in which device spectrum mode was performed by the NaI(Tl) (sodium iodide doped with thallium) scintillation detector (3″ × 3″) and dose rate mode was measured by GM (Geiger-Muller) Tube (Pancake) for these standard gamma sources. The spectral analysis of measured energy (MeV), count rate (cps) and dose rates (μSv/h) have been determined for the confirmation of the results by the PHITS simulation and experimental work with the same geometry according to the radial distance with a minimum of 10 cm to maximum of 100 cm from gamma source and detector. All of these gamma sources have been found to be safe to use in academic research because the dose rates for each distance, are calculated for the safety amount that ensures all practices are conducted in compliance with the radiation safety regulation not exceeding the limit of 20 mSv per year. The findings underscore the importance of advanced simulation tools in enhancing radiation safety regulation and contribute to the broader understanding of nuclear physics.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis on Phrase-Based Statistical Machine Translation and Operation Sequence Model for Myanmar-English Machine Translation
abstract: Statistical Machine Translation (SMT) is the mapping between a source language and a target language from parallel corpora which are sets of texts in both languages that are aligned at the sentence level. SMT relies on the probability distributions of linguistic units and their corresponding translations derived from this aligned data. Certain Myanmar phrases and expressions require multiple words to be rearranged or split when translated into English. This paper presents the Phrase-Based Statistical Machine Translation (PBSMT) and an enhanced approach leveraging the Operation Sequence Model (OSM) with an adjustable distortion limit. The two translation models are optimized to improve translation accuracy by accommodating different reordering patterns inherent in Myanmar-English translation. By setting an adjustable distortion limit, the models can more flexibly adjust the order of phrases to better match natural English syntax and ungrammatical translations. This approach offers a significant result for Myanmar-English SMT systems and addresses critical issues in linguistic alignment and reordering. Myanmar-English parallel corpus 85K is used as data statistics for both syllable and word level segmentations. The system performance is evaluated by BLEU scores on 80% 10% 10% for training, validation and testing respectively. Experimental results indicate that the OSM model with extended distortion limit significantly enhances translation quality, providing greater fluency and grammatical coherence in the target language.

articleTitle: A Graph Neural Diffusion Network for Sophisticated Persistent Threat Hunting in IoT Environments
abstract: Sophisticated Persistent Threats (SPTs) in IoT environments exhibit strong concealment, extended durations, and rapid evolution, making traditional passive detection methods inadequate for effective threat identification. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a Threat Hunting model based on a Graph Neural Diffusion Network (GNDN), which excels in capturing multi-scale relationships and dynamic features within IoT systems. The model transforms input Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) log graphs and IoT kernel audit log graphs into enriched graph representations. A GNDN layer is employed to diffuse critical information across graph nodes, capturing both local and global dependencies. Furthermore, a pre-trained Transformer encoder fine-tuned for temporal and positional encoding processes these enriched graphs to enhance feature representation. Finally, similarity scores are calculated through attention-based graph matching to identify SPT traces. Experiments conducted in a simulated IoT environment demonstrate that the proposed GNDN model reduces mean squared error by approximately 22%, increases Spearman rank correlation by 1.3%, and improves matching accuracy by around 2.0% compared to state-of-the-art graph neural networks.

articleTitle: Abnormal Fall Detection by Hybrid Deep Learning Model
abstract: Fall detection is crucial for various applications such as elderly care, healthcare, smart homes, workplace safety, and wearables and edge devices. Deep learning, a subset of machine learning, uses neural networks to analyze data and recognize patterns, making it a powerful tool for fall detection. Deep learning-based fall detection systems have been the subject of much research, however issues with accuracy and robustness, real-time processing, privacy and ethical issues, multimodal integration, and dataset limits still exist. This paper aims to address these challenges and focuses on abnormal fall detection systems. The system utilizes a hybrid deep learning approach combining VGG16 and LSTM networks to improve the detection of fall behaviors. The results indicate that integrating the VGG16 with LSTM improves the fall detection performance and achieves a testing accuracy of 95%.

articleTitle: Leveraging K-means Clustering for Multi-objective Task Scheduling in Cloud-based Scientific Workflows
abstract: In the cloud environment, efficient task scheduling for scientific workflows presents significant challenges, especially when addressing multiple conflicting objectives such as minimizing execution time and cost. This study proposes a novel multiobjective task scheduling approach utilizing the K-means clustering algorithm, tailored for optimizing the Montage, and Sipht, well-known scientific workflows. K-means enhances resource allocation by grouping tasks with similar characteristics, enabling better load balancing and scalability. Experimental results demonstrate notable improvements in makespan and total execution time compared to traditional scheduling methods. This work underscores the potential of the proposed approach to advance task scheduling techniques for scientific workflows, paving the way for broader applications in the cloud environment.

articleTitle: Motion-Resilient Deep Learning for ECG Signal Classification: A Multi-Electrode Approach Using Adaptive Feature Extraction
abstract: Wearable ECG monitoring systems are finding applications in continuous health surveillance. However, motion artifacts typically destroy the signal’s integrity and degrade diagnostic accuracy. In this research, we present a newly developed deep-learning framework that mitigates motion-induced signal degradation by exploiting multi-electrode spatial redundancy and adaptive feature extraction techniques. In this work, a convolutional recurrent neural network is proposed to classify four electrode configurations over different physical activities, as recorded in the MACECGDB database. A new type of multistage feature extraction strategy has been developed that integrates time-domain, frequency-domain, and motion-correlated features within a dynamic reconstruction of ECG signals using the proposed model with enhanced noise robustness. Experimental results have confirmed accuracy in the classification of standing, walking, and jumping conditions well above the traditionally used methods of artifact reduction. This work further enhances the reliability of ambulatory ECG monitoring by integrating machine learning into sophisticated signal processing techniques to provide a robust solution for real-world physiological signal analysis in mobile health applications.

articleTitle: The Risks & Realities of Picking an IoT OS
abstract: Internet of Things is no longer a new topic. Long ago, the network of things was a rare thing which could be seen only in offices, industries, and labs. Nowadays it is approaching becoming a ubiquitous appliance as a commonplace in everyday environments. Homes and public places such as traffic and city parks have changed to adapt with things within the ability to connect to a network. As a result, even commoners are becoming familiar with IoT. Researchers lay the new technologies into IoT networks. Developers drive them into industry and practitioners carry the aesthetic essence by carrying on the practice among people. In doing so, choosing the correct operating system for the correct device is a step not to be skipped as the learning curve grows up to advanced. This study aims to aid the practitioners by discussing the risks and realities concerned with the role of OS in IoT devices or systems.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Intensity Transformation Methods for Dark Alarm Container X-ray Image Enhancement
abstract: X-ray scanning machines are being utilized by customs organizations for efficient container inspection, but Dark Alarm (DA) of X-ray images indicates an inability to penetrate an object. Physical checks are advised for DA containers, as they can significantly hinder trade facilitation. Thus, image manipulation is essential for enhancement of these DA images, and it is employed to increase human operators' accuracy. In this paper, an experimental study is carried out to evaluate the performance of three famous intensity transformation methods: Adaptive Histogram Equalization (AHE), Logarithmic Transform, and Square-Root Transform. Various DA container images are tested with these techniques and required decision can be made for DA container X-ray images enhancement. Experimental result shows that Logarithmic Transform is better than two intensity transforms in almost all the DA cargo X-ray images.

articleTitle: Analysis of Long-term Electricity Demand Prediction in Myanmar
abstract: The population of Myanmar grew at 1.0% per year from 41.3 million in 1990 to 55.8 million in 2022. Although the relationship between population and electricity consumption is complex and multifaceted, and influenced by economic development, technological advancements, energy efficiency, and lifestyle patterns, the population increases, the demand for electricity typically rises. This paper introduces the prediction of electricity consumption model based on population varies by region such as rural and urban area of Myanmar using time series analysis. The proposed work is intended to propose the long-term prediction of electricity consumption. Three models such as a simple autoregressive model, ARIMA, two deep learning models, GRU, and LSTM are developed and analyzed in this paper. This study evaluates the accuracy of predicted outcomes to identify the most suitable model for long-term electricity consumption forecasting, based on the population percentage of densely populated and hottest cities in Myanmar.

articleTitle: Real-Time CO2 Concentration Monitoring Across Various Environments in Mandalay
abstract: The purpose of this research is to develop a system that provides real-time alerts to the residents of Mandalay in the event of hazardous air quality conditions, enabling prompt awareness and response to potential health risks. In addition to Carbon-dioxide levels at Mandalay Technological University (MTU), key urban CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>and suburban areas of Mandalay, including major transportation hubs like highway bus terminals and train stations, are monitored. CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> conditions in these areas are monitored and analyzed using TTGO Call ESP with Wi-Fi modules microcontrollers and DM118 CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> sensor. The DM118 offers continuous CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> measurement, providing real-time data, which is crucial for applications. This feature supports dynamic environmental monitoring where timely responses to air quality changes are essential. A solar energy system as a renewable power source is utilized in the research. The data from DM118 CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> sensor is transmitted to the ESP32 microcontroller, displayed on a 16*2 LCD display with I2C interface and uploaded to the PythonAnywhere cloud server for remote monitoring and analysis of air quality in real-time. The CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> data from three locations in Mandalay for October 2024 were obtained from the PythonAnywhere server, downloaded as CSV files and analyzed and compared using charts. The accuracy was calculated by comparing the values measured by ECD MDY.

Author Keywords: TTGO Call ESP 32 with Wi-Fi Module

articleTitle: Classifying Real versus AI Generated Images using CIFAR-10 Network and Painting Image Data
abstract: The proliferation of AI-generated images, particularly in the domain of digital art, has raised significant challenges in distinguishing real content from synthetic creations. This research explores distinguishing between real and AI-generated images using art-painting datasets. A convolutional neural network (CNN)-based approach is proposed to classify images as either real or AI-generated, leveraging the CIFAR-10 network architecture for the task. The AI-generated paintings are produced using generative models such as GANs to simulate a wide range of artistic styles. Through rigorous training and evaluation, the results demonstrate the capacity and effectiveness of deep learning models in distinguishing between real and synthetic images. According to the comparing results of the CNN network and CIFAR-10 network, the accuracy of CIFAR-10 network is higher than the CNN network. The findings highlight model robustness in the detection of AI-generated content, providing insights into the future of automated content verification and digital forensics.

articleTitle: Multi-Head Attention Based LSTM Model for Forecasting Bangladeshi Stock Market Prices
abstract: Forecasting stock prices is crucial for investment and risk management, offering insights into market trends and aiding investors in making informed decisions. Traditional time-series models, such as LSTM and GRU, have demonstrated promise in capturing temporal dependencies within stock market data. However, these models often fall short in identifying complex patterns due to limited attention mechanisms, particularly in emerging markets with unique economic factors like the Bangla stock market. Addressing this gap, we propose a novel Multi-Head Attention and LSTM-based architecture that combines the sequential processing capabilities of LSTM with multi-head attention layers to better capture contextual dependencies and subtle fluctuations in stock price movements. Our approach is evaluated on datasets from six major Bangladeshi banks, including Islami Bank, Dhaka Bank, Arab Bangladesh (AB) Bank, Bank Asia, Eastern Bank Limited (EBL), and City Bank. Results demonstrate that our model outperforms traditional models across all metrics. The integration of multi-head attention allows for nuanced attention allocation across time steps, significantly enhancing forecasting accuracy. This enhanced model can serve as a valuable tool for investors and financial analysts, supporting better forecasting for risk assessment and investment strategy formulation. The framework demonstrates potential scalability across other emerging markets, offering an adaptable solution for financial forecasting in regions with complex market dynamics.

articleTitle: Exploring Transfer Learning in a Bidirectional Myanmar-Tedim Chin Machine Translation with the mT5 Transformer
abstract: Machine translation (MT) plays a crucial role in bridging linguistic gaps, particularly for underrepresented languages. This paper investigates the feasibility and performance of the mT5-transformer model in machine translation task from Myanmar to Tedim Chin and Tedim Chin to Myanmar language respectively. The experiment conduct on the 10K parallel corpus from UCSY dataset that contain different domain such as greetings, stories (from educational books), communication, leisure (traveling, shopping, nightlife), and resources (numbers, time, and accuracy). In data collection stage, we firstly collect 10K Myanmar sentences from UCSY corpus, and then, translate it into Tedim Chin language and finally create our own Myanmar-Tedim Chin corpus. On the other hand, Myanmar text is written without explicit spaces between words, making segmentation a challenging an essential step. Therefore, we preprocess the dataset using the customized syllable and word level segmentation approaches for Myanmar language and then fine-tune it on the mT5 model using that dataset, and finally evaluate the performance of the proposed model with the BLEU scores and accuracy. From all experiments, we can see that the model performance on the syllable level gets the outperform result than the word level approach. Therefore, comparing the result on both translations on syllable segmentation, the score for the experiment show that the Myanmar-Tedim Chin translation gives better result than the Tedim Chin-Myanmar translation by increasing 0.10% on BLEU score and 0.07% on the accuracy score. Tedim Chin is a low-resource language and the final result shows that the mT5 transformer work pretty well on Tedim Chin and also in Myanmar text.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Coverless Video Steganography for Secret Audio
abstract: Coverless video steganography has emerged as a promising technique for covert communication, offering a high level of security by avoiding direct modification of media content. In this research, a proposed system is implemented for Coverless Video Steganography that leverages Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) features to securely embed secret audio information within video content without altering the cover media. This proposed method first extracts robust MFCC features from the secret audio, capturing perceptually relevant speech characteristics. These features are then mapped to semantically similar visual features within selected frames of a cover video through a CNN-based feature matching process, ensuring that the embedded information is not directly detectable. For enhanced security, the audio secret information is encrypted using RSA encryption before embedding, providing an additional layer of protection against unauthorized access. By integrating MFCC and CNN features with RSA encryption, this method effectively ensures the security and imperceptibility of secret data within the video. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high security, strong resilience against steganalysis attacks, and effective data retrieval accuracy, marking it as a viable solution for secure, undetectable audio communication. This proposed system applied for Secure Medical Record. In this system, embeds sensitive audio medical data, such as diagnostic results or doctor’s notes, into patient video files for secure and private storage or sharing with the better security performance.

articleTitle: Scalable Serverless Architecture for Delivering Personalized Recommendations
abstract: Recently, serverless computing has transformed the mode of development for scalable, cost-effective solutions for a great many applications. We are suggesting a scalable architecture for serving personalized recommendations that is based on native cloud services and microservices. This architecture dynamically allocates resources according to user demands in a scenario of lower operating costs with still high performance. Personalized recommendation systems have been of great importance to businesses, particularly in e-commerce, content streaming, and social platforms. Of course, the complexity lies in making all these recommendations available in real-time to millions of users without overloading the system. The serverless approach of this architecture decouples those core processing components, allowing individual microservices to scale independently based on traffic and computational demand. The system uses event-driven triggers for processing data and model inference as well as to generate a response, allowing for flexibility in a powerful way to grow workloads. We evaluate this architecture on several use cases, concentrated on the ones for e-commerce and content recommendation. Using both collaborative filtering and content-based approaches, we were able to achieve considerable improvements in terms of system scalability and low response times while reducing operational overheads.

articleTitle: Hybrid BERT, CNN-BILSTM Model for Detecting Self-Admitted Technical Debt in Software Development
abstract: Software developers frequently take shortcuts during the software development process, which they document as self-admitted technical debt (SATD) through source code comments. While SATD enhances transparency since developers acknowledge its presence through source code comments, it significantly increases software maintenance costs, elevates defect rates, degrades software quality and poses security vulnerabilities. To address these issues, we propose a state-of-the-art hybrid machine learning model that integrates BERT, CNN and BiLSTM architectures with attention for the automated detection of self-admitted technical debt. We use BERT for contextual embeddings, BiLSTM for capturing sequential dependencies and CNN to capture local patterns. Employing an experimental approach, our model achieved an average F1-score of 0.78 with attention, an improvement when compared with our baseline models. The contribution of this paper is a high-performing hybrid machine learning model for the automatic detection of technical debt leading to better software quality and low maintenance cost.

articleTitle: Enhancing Water Safety in the Philippines: Early Detection of Drowning Patterns through Wearable Devices and Machine Learning Algorithms
abstract: Drowning, described as the process of respiratory impairment/failure or suffocation due to submersion in water, remains one of the leading causes of preventable injury worldwide. Early intervention is crucial in reducing morbidity and mortality, as quick alerts and rapid response times are able to significantly lower the risk of permanent injury or death. The implementation of an automated system for detection and alerting of drowning patterns would then prove to have significant benefits to public health and safety. The researchers aim to create a system which can perform drowning detection through the use of technology that has become more ubiquitous in recent years, smartwatches. Smartwatches are compact mobile devices which are worn on the wrist that also may come with a variety of features and sensor technology. This study aims to both discuss and test the feasibility of using programmable smartwatches as a medium for reliable, affordable, and accurate detection of drowning patterns in real world scenarios. Collection of biometric data in real time will be used in tandem with machine learning algorithms such as the Local Outlier Factor (LOF) in order to detect anomalies in biometric data that may signal that a user is exhibiting symptoms of drowning. Furthermore, the study will also explore the challenges, limitations, and feasibility associated with the creation and implementation of the automated drowning detection system, including the need for accurate data collection, machine learning algorithm optimizations, and system validation and testing in real world scenarios. The potential applications of the proposed system may extend beyond individual user monitoring and may also have implications for improving current water safety measures among vulnerable groups, which could ultimately reduce the burden placed on water safety groups by drowning incidents.

articleTitle: Evaluating Word2Vec and WordNet for Semantic Similarity at Myanmar Word and Sentence Levels
abstract: One of the most important NLP processes is word embedding, which converts words into numerical vectors for various NLP tasks. Although Word2Vec has been widely used for word embeddings in the Myanmar language, WordNet is a more recent approach. This study evaluates Word2Vec and WordNet in assessing semantic similarity at both the word and sentence levels in the Myanmar language. Word2Vec, which leverages a neural network, is effective at capturing contextual relationships and sentence-level similarity. In contrast, WordNet, a structured semantic database, excels at word-level similarity by leveraging its ontological structure, though it lacks contextual depth for sentences. To address WordNet's lack of support for Myanmar, text is translated into English using Google Translate. The analysis shows that WordNet performs better at word-level tasks requiring semantic structure, while Word2Vec excels in capturing sentence-level context, providing complementary strengths for Myanmar NLP tasks. These findings provide valuable insights for NLP tasks in Myanmar.

articleTitle: The Information Systems and Model for Succession Planning in Higher Education Institutions
abstract: Succession planning is important in organization management. It is a strategic level management that involves not only finding the best successor but also including the development program for the successor so that they will be ready for the new prospective position. The integration and collaboration between all related stakeholders are important. Specifically, in succession planning at higher education, key positions play an important role so that institutional operations can run well. In this research, a succession planning model in higher education was built using the Systematic Literature Review(SLR), and the Software Development Lifecycle(SDLC) method was used for the application development, also, to be able to evaluate the implementation of one of the steps of the model, the simulation technique used machine learning (ML) to find the best algorithm for predicting the readiness of potential successors at higher education. Six algorithms were used: Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, K-Nearest Neighbor, Linear Discriminant Analysis, Gaussian Naïve Bayes, and Support Vector Machine. The data prepared for the simulation is based on the factors for the best successor candidate. The results obtained in this research are the succession planning model and the application design, as well as the Support Vector Machine (SVM) algorithm as the best algorithm for predicting the readiness status of successor candidates based on SVM’s accuracy score that is compared to the other algorithm in some variance amounts of data. The Succession Planning Model that is actualized in the application design provides a reference for the higher education institution to implement the Succession Model in their institution.

articleTitle: MyanSpeech: Joint CTC-Attention and RNN Language Model for End-To-End Read Speech Recognition
abstract: This paper proposed MyanSpeech<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>, an end-to-end Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) system designed for the Myanmar language, exploiting a joint CTC-Attention architecture for the acoustic model in combination with a Recurrent Neural Network Language Model (RNN-LM). The integration of CTC-Attention addresses the challenge of aligning audio with text in Myanmar, effectively combining the strengths of Connectionist Temporal Classification (CTC) for stable framewise alignment with Attention mechanisms for handling longer dependencies and variable input lengths. This dual approach enhances recognition accuracy, particularly for low-resource languages. The RNN-LM further supports the model by capturing language-specific grammar and contextual relationships. The dataset includes 36 hours, 33 minutes, and 51 seconds of read speech from 20 males and 18 females speakers, comprising 35,468 utterances of daily conversation from the Linguistic Committee (LC). Among various configurations, the best models achieved a word error rate (WER) of 7.093% and character error rate (CER) of 4.474% on a speaker-dependent (closed test), and a WER of 26.829% and CER of 17.597% on a speaker-independent (open test), respectively. These results highlight the effectiveness of integrating CTC-Attention and RNN-LM for Myanmar ASR, offering a reliable solution for speech recognition in low-resource language.

articleTitle: Smoke Detection for Natural Disaster Prevention and Environment Protection
abstract: Climate change poses a significant threat, contributing to the emergence of forest fire hotspots in Myanmar. These fires result in severe air pollution, impacting the environment. Whether caused by natural disasters or human activities, such as burning trash or discarding lit cigarettes, it is crucial to implement a forest fire hotspot monitoring system. The primary objective of this system is to identify areas of forest fires, particularly in regions with dense tree growth, caused by both natural events and human actions. Utilizing a YOLOv8 smoke detection model, the system effectively detects smoke, making it a valuable tool for monitoring and investigating forest fires. We construct the forest fire dataset by ourselves in this system. The system is able to preserve the natural environment due to the timely reporting system. Minimizing damages reducing air pollution. Beyond these benefits, using IoT technologies (YOLOv8) based on virtual imagery, detect forest fires in time, as well as air pollution conditions in the environment, and it is a useful system for preventing natural disasters.

articleTitle: Enhancing Cebuano Constituency Parsing: A Stemmer and Syntax Tree Optimization Approach
abstract: The Philippines, having over 170 languages, faces language barriers and diminished language fluency due to heavy English influence and the effects of globalization. The language focuses on Cebuano, the second most spoken language mainly spoken in Central Visayas. Existing Cebuano parsers have been made through Recursive Descent Parsing (RDP) for a Cebuano Parse Tree in relaying grammar through a syntactic structure. However, there were identified limitations through low-level sentences, lacking grammar codes, low metric score, and stemmer evaluation errors. To address this gap, the researchers proposed a Snowball-based stemmer approach along with the Cocke-Kasami-Younger algorithm and additional grammar codes for better syntax tree optimization. Due to the lack of a dataset for Cebuano sentences, the Cebuano Corpus is extensively created by the researchers via web scraping and data augmentation techniques such as language dialect filtration and sentence range variation. The dataset comprises at least 500 collected phrases to be annotated by the linguist experts for the Gold Standard Parse Treebank (GSPT). The GSPT will serve as the parser's benchmark through syntax constituents, known as the PARSEVAL metric system. The improved parser attained an accuracy of 82.14%, suggesting a high rate of correct Cebuano constituents from a Cebuano sentence. The findings suggest that the developed system is more effective than its predecessor. By leveraging advanced Snowball-based algorithms and updated Grammar Codes, the study demonstrates the potential of parsers in preserving cultural language.

articleTitle: Profiling Mushrooms in the Philippines Using Ensemble Transfer Learning
abstract: Profiling mushrooms in the Philippines is crucial for their conservation, contributions to different fields of study, and raising health awareness regarding edible and non-edible species. The identification of mushrooms faces several challenges, including environmental climate conditions, the introduction of non-native species, and the variability in mushroom appearances across the country. To address these challenges, this study introduces an ensemble transfer learning model utilizing ResNet50, InceptionV3, and EfficientNet-B5 models. These models, pre-trained on ImageNet, have shown significant accuracy in image classification while maintaining a balance of efficiency and cost. The models are trained using 8,000 samples from the Mushroom Observer dataset as well as images of mushrooms collected from the Philippines. A stacked ensemble technique is employed, and XGBoost is used as the meta-model to combine the base models' predictions. The testing results achieved an accuracy of 94.25%, with precision at 92.08%, recall at 96.83%, and an F1-score of 94.39%. These results show the strength of the ensemble model in identifying the edibility of various mushroom species. This study contributes to advancements in image classification models and machine learning techniques, with a focus on promoting informed mushroom consumption and enhancing awareness across fields of study.

articleTitle: Digital Twin Implementation for Turntable Systems in Automated Bottle Production
abstract: This paper explores the design and implementation of a digital twin for a bottle production line, focusing on the turntable system used in feeding operations. Turntables play a critical role in dispatching products one by one from bulk, and are widely used in bottle filling and capping machines. We developed a simplified 3D model of the turntable, which interacts with bottles in a simulated environment based on real-world physics. The goal was to enhance industrial automation by simulating physical interactions using advanced techniques, including C# scripting, and providing a foundation for integrating digital twins in manufacturing systems. Key experiments demonstrated the model’s ability to evaluate bottle stability under varying gravity, rotational speeds, and controlled spawning conditions, offering insights for optimizing turntable operations.

articleTitle: Fine Tuning the BART Model for Mon-English Neural Machine Translation
abstract: Fine-tuning large pre-trained models has been proven successful for many tasks in NLP. This paper describes the procedures for adapting the target language neural machine translation (NMT) for Mon-English using BART (Bidirectional and Auto-Regressive Transformers) model fine-tuning. The goal of this paper has been translated Mon, which is considered to be a lesser-resourced language, to English fine tuning with BART model. This paper analyzes the performance of the BART model while employing it in machine translation from Mon to English on a parallel corpus of 25k parallel sentences. There are two ways of preparing the Mon language. First, the Mon text was tokenized using a mon vocabulary mapping whereas the English text used the BART tokenizer. This setting has attained a BLEU score of 30.14, which reflects moderate translation quality. In the second approach, the Mon text was tokenized using a SentencePiece-based Byte Pair Encoding (BPE) model and the English text still used the BART tokenizer. This resulted in significantly higher translation performance, with a BLEU score of 38.72, proving that the application of SentencePiece BPE in tokenizing Mon text combined with the BART tokenizer for English was successful. These results show that the choice of tokenization method for the source language has an essential role in improving machine translation performance for low-resource languages like Mon.

articleTitle: Integrating Vision Transformers with Support Vector Machines for Video Classification
abstract: Video classification has wide applications in surveillance, sports analysis, content recommendation, and more, making it is important to model the spatial and temporal dynamics accurately. The standard convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have proven to be excellent in spatial feature extraction but are less competent in modeling temporal relationships. This is one of the biggest problems with these models not being able to model long-range dependencies, which has led to the development of Vision Transformers (ViTs). However, their application in video classification remains underexplored. In this paper, the problem of improving the accuracy of video classification is approached by combining the strengths of ViTs and traditional classifiers. A pre-trained Vision Transformer is used to obtain high-dimensional feature representations, which are then integrated with a Support Vector Machine (SVM) that performs the classification. But the results of our experiment show that our ViT-SVM combination actually overcomes traditional methods and is thus a fairly competitive approach with a higher accuracy rate. These results suggest the possibility of using hybrid models to improve the accuracy of video classification.

articleTitle: Revitalizing the Power of Blockchain Implementation for Transaction Processes in Real Estate Sector
abstract: Real estate is one of the most profitable assets in the world because it has advantages or significant impacts in the broader community, such as financial security, capable investment opportunities, economic stability, and growing the economy by empowering welfare and individual or corporate ownership through its transaction activities. But behind all these advantages, real estate transactions often face challenges such as high costs, lack of transparency and dependence on third parties. These problems will spread to other aspects, such as inefficient transactions because of the many entities that want to contribute, document falsification due to lack of transparency and disputes that can damage trust between stakeholders. Therefore, maintaining the security and validity of transaction documents is very much needed to minimize existing problems. To overcome these problems, applying blockchain technology in real estate transactions was proposed to create a safer, more transparent and efficient system. With blockchain's decentralized and immutable nature, it can overcome dependence on third parties and the problem of fraud risk. Supported by smart contracts and tokenization, blockchain enables the automation of transaction processes, thereby reducing costs, increasing speed, and strengthening trust at every transaction stage which can be more efficient and reliable.

articleTitle: PrecisionStroke: Optimized Stroke Risk Prediction through Advanced Hyperparameter Tuning and Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: Stroke prediction is a challenging problem in the healthcare domain, especially due to high class imbalance in datasets where data about stroke cases is a very small portion. In this study we develop a machine learning based framework for stroke prediction that tackles through powerful data preprocessing methods, such as Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) for balancing the classes. (Situated within the entire framework of a comparative evaluation of the Random Forest, Support Vector Machine (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), CatBoost, XGBoost, LightGBM, and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) and TabNet machine learning classifiers as per unique designs. In conclusion, the Random Forest classifier proved to be the best performing model with an accuracy of 99.38%, followed closely by LightGBM and CatBoost. A detailed analysis including KP song metrics including precision, F1 score, and confusion matrices were carried out to ensure thorough evaluation. The study also emphasizes the importance of explainable AI tools which improve the explainability of predictions. This framework shows that machine learning has the potential to assist with early detection of stroke and may ultimately be integrated into clinical decision-making systems.

articleTitle: The Role of AI-Based Teaching Assistants in Enhancing Student Engagement and Academic Performance in Indonesian Higher Education
abstract: Artificial intelligence-based teaching assistants (AITAs) offer an innovative solution to improve the quality of higher education in Indonesia through personalized learning, real-time feedback, and automation of administrative tasks. This technology has proven effective in developed countries in improving student engagement and teaching efficiency. In Indonesia, AITAs have great potential, especially in STEM fields, despite facing challenges such as limited infrastructure, low digital literacy, and lack of regulation. To maximize the benefits, investment in technology, user training, and policies that support the ethical adoption of AI are needed. Collaboration between governments, educational institutions, and technology providers is needed to create a more inclusive and competitive higher education system in the digital era.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Models for Analyzing Gait Dynamics in Neurodegenerative Diseases
abstract: Gait analysis can be very useful for the early detection and monitoring of neurodegenerative diseases as discussed; such changes in gait dynamics normally appear before the initial clinical symptoms. Hence, a deep learning-based framework is developed to analyze gait patterns using the time-series data of wearable sensors. Therefore, a hybrid model using Long Short-Term Memory Networks and Convolutional Neural Networks is further proposed in this paper for the classification of foot strike events from temporal gait features. Padded sequence and one-hot label encoding for binary classification were done on the pre-processing of stride and swing interval and other spatiotemporal gait measures. Standard metrics in classification can be used to measure the performance of the models. An accuracy of 85% with an ROC curve area of 0.91 was seen. These findings thus confirm the potentiality of deep learning models to classify gait dynamics with high precision and further indicate their promise as a useful tool for monitoring the course of neurodegenerative diseases such as Parkinson’s disease and Alzheimer’s. Our work underlines the importance of machine learning in health applications, opening up new avenues toward early detection and intervention.

articleTitle: Federated Learning with Secure Aggregation for Privacy-Preserving Deep Learning in IoT Environments
abstract: To effectively handle the massive data generated by large-scale IoT applications, deep learning has been widely applied in IoT environments. However, deep models face security threats such as inference attacks and model reverse-engineering during the training process, which can lead to the leakage of original data fed into the model. Federated Learning (FL) with Secure Aggregation offers a robust solution to this issue by enabling distributed model training without sharing raw data. This method ensures privacy by securely aggregating model updates from IoT devices, mitigating risks of data exposure during transmission. To further enhance model performance, a regularization term is introduced to address overfitting and facilitate the learning of significant features. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach effectively enhances the generalization capability of the model. As the number of iterations increases, the accuracy difference between the FL-trained model and the model trained on centralized data remains below 0.5%. Therefore, the proposed method not only protects user privacy but also ensures model usability, achieving a balance between privacy and utility.

articleTitle: Systematic Comparison of Vectorization Methods in Topic Classification for Myanmar Language
abstract: Text classification which is a research area of text data mining is widely used and one of the popular tasks of Natural Language Processing (NLP). But very few had focused on the effective use of vectorization methods which are vital in classification systems. In this paper, three widely used vectorizers for topic classification are discussed. The main goal is to evaluate the effectiveness of three different vectorization techniques such as TF-IDF Vectorizer (TFID), Count Vectorizer, and Word2Vec Vectorizer in the context of Myanmar news topic classification. The study focuses on a dataset comprising Myanmar news articles categorized into four distinct topics: Politics, Entertainment, Crime, and Business. Each category has 180 unique articles and in total 720 articles are prepared. Furthermore, these articles undergo segmentation and preprocessing. Each vectorization technique is applied through experimentation on an RBF (Radial Basis Function) Support Vector Machine (SVM) model. Moreover, feature selection via Chi Square algorithm is applied to optimize performance. Results indicate that TFID outperforms the other vectorizers, as seen by its accuracy of 83% on the test set, compared to 75% for the Count vectorizer and 48% for the Word2Vec. Overall, this research contributes insights into the effective utilization of NLP techniques for Myanmar news classification by emphasizing the advantage of TFID Vectorization compared to other vectorization techniques.

articleTitle: Generative AI for Real-Time Cloud Security: Advanced Anomaly Detection Using GPT Models
abstract: As cloud infrastructures become increasingly complex and integral to modern enterprises, the demand for advanced, real-time security solutions has grown significantly. Traditional anomaly detection systems often struggle to keep pace with the rapid evolution of cyber threats in these dynamic environments, particularly when faced with novel or sophisticated attacks. Such systems typically rely on predefined rules or signature-based detection, which limits their effectiveness in identifying emerging security risks. This paper explores the potential of generative AI models, specifically LLaMA and OpenAI’s GPT architectures, to enhance real-time cloud security. By leveraging the advanced pattern recognition and adaptive capabilities of these models, we propose a framework that can analyze vast amounts of cloud data, including logs, network traffic, user behavior, and system activities, to detect abnormal patterns indicative of security threats. The real-time anomaly detection offered by generative AI provides a significant advantage over traditional methods, as it continuously learns from new data, thereby improving its ability to identify novel threats in complex cloud environments.This research addresses key gaps in current cloud security practices, highlighting the limitations of existing systems in detecting previously unknown threats. The proposed approach introduces generative AI as a highly adaptive and scalable solution for cloud anomaly detection, capable of responding to evolving threats in real-time. By using models such as GPT, which are known for their ability to generate coherent predictions based on diverse inputs, the framework offers a novel means of safe-guarding cloud infrastructure. This study not only underscores the benefits of employing generative AI for security purposes but also provides a robust methodology for integrating these models into cloud security systems. The paper concludes with an assessment of the practical deployment of these AI models in large-scale cloud environments, demonstrating their potential to significantly enhance the resilience and adaptability of modern cloud security frameworks.

articleTitle: Automated Prediction of Bug Reports' Severity using Attention-based Convolutional Neural Network
abstract: Bug report severity attribute is critical for developers in deciding the level of impact or seriousness of a bug. Developers must accurately specify the severity level because the impact of bugs affects the Bug Triage process. This process is essential in maintaining and developing software. Researchers proposed many related works with bug severity prediction to improve the software maintenance process. Most of the previous studies use many different techniques in the determination of severity levels. However, these works still need to improve the prediction performance. This work attempts to use an attention-based Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to estimate bug reports' severity levels efficiently. Firstly, the unstructured text for each bug report from Eclipse and Mozilla projects of the Bugzilla Bug Tracking System (BTS) is preprocessed by using Natural Language Processing techniques. Then, the preprocessed text is represented as embedded vectors using the word2vec (skip-gram model). Finally, the vectorized inputs feed into the attention-based CNN model to extract features and the model predicts the levels of severity for each bug report. The proposed model develops the prediction performance by adding a scaled dot-product attention mechanism into a simple CNN model. In this paper, accuracy, precision, recall, and f1-score are used to assess the performance using a confusion matrix. The experimental findings proved that the attention-based CNN model enhances the prediction metrics by up to 1.09%, 3.93%, 1.09%, and 3.29% respectively by using an attention layer in the conventional CNN model.
